A LIFETIME OF PURPOSE IN FLIGHT. ✈️🧭

Five decades in aviation—and a career spent putting an airplane to good use.

General Aviation News reported November 16 that commercial pilot and conservationist David S. Smith has earned the FAA Wright Brothers Master Pilot Award.

Smith first soloed in October 1972. His flying has included tracking wildlife in the American West, bringing relief supplies to isolated communities in Honduras and using general aviation for aerial mapping and conservation work through CAVU.

CAVU’s own biography documents his bush-pilot background and hundreds of conservation overflights. It’s a reminder of what small aircraft can make possible when a pilot has a purpose beyond the destination.

Congratulations, David—here’s to a lifetime of skill, service and careful flying. 💛

Sources: General Aviation News, November 16, 2026; CAVU biography.
